name: IBM 5151 monochrome display with a P3 amber phosphor (MDA raster)

timing.ref: IBM BIOS 6845 parameters for the MDA (R0 61h, R4 19h, R5 06h, R9 0Dh) and the 16.257 MHz dot clock; 5151: 50 Hz, 18.432 kHz, 350 lines (Wikipedia, IBM 5151)

drive.mapping: level = floor(3 (1 - luma) + 0.5) / 3: dark art drives the beam
drive.ref: MDA video pin = 2/3, intensity pin = 1/3 of the luminance (Wikipedia, IBM Monochrome Display Adapter). Content is free, so the TTL signal may switch anywhere along a line.

phosphor.efficiency_ref: Tektronix relative luminance (via Jankowiak): P3 45, P4 70
facts: P3: zinc beryllium silicate with manganese (Zn8BeSi5O19:Mn); yellow fluorescence and phosphorescence (JEDEC/EIA, via Jankowiak)
peak 602 nm; 10 % of the peak at 504 and 700 nm
exponential (one Mn2+ transition), 13 ms to 10 %; RCA's zinc beryllium silicate gives 12.5 ms
x 0.528 y 0.458, dominant 584 nm: CIE 1931 colour of a band through the three published points. As a band in photon energy instead: x 0.487 y 0.500
just outside sRGB: moved toward grey at its true luminance where needed
short: a moving piece leaves almost no trail; the light ripples at 50 Hz on a real tube (not visible here: the display shows the average over each refresh)
amber monitors are commonly said to use P3; many 1980s amber monitors used P134, which has no published data
the same full-drive luminance as the P39 profile; none published for P3
refs: Jankowiak, Cathode Ray Tube Phosphors Of Interest To The Experimenter (P3: 602 nm, 504-700 nm, 13 ms, Zn8BeSi5O19:Mn; exponential-decay screens P1, P3, P12, P13)
RCA TPM-1508A Phosphors for Cathode-Ray Tubes (Oct 1961): zinc beryllium silicate:Mn, 12.5 ms to 10 %

colour.note: One layer; its true linear-sRGB colour per unit luminance (blue slightly negative: just outside the display), brought into the gamut per pixel.

spot.ref: Philips M31-336/338/350: about 1300 lines over 201 mm (shrinking raster, 68.5 cd/m2, phosphor W); flat-field pitch = 2 sigma
spot.line_count_height_note: Philips measures the 1300 lines on a 216 x 162 mm raster without saying which height the count refers to; over 162 mm the line width would be 0.125 mm. 201 mm (the useful height) is used.

bloom.model: sigma(drive) = sigma_mm * (drive / efficiency_vs_P4) ** power; drive = beam signal relative to full drive, held at min_drive_fraction or above (the measured currents span a factor of 4)
bloom.ref: Philips T16 1987, Resolution characteristics, Fig. 5 (M31-336..350, 12 kV): line width at 50, 75, 100, 200 uA, traced into tools/philips-m31-line-width.json

raster.note: raster assumed to fill the useful height of a Philips 31 cm 90 degree monitor tube; the 5151's own picture size is not published

etch.model: front reflection = Fresnel x (specular_fraction x mirror image of the room light + the rest blurred by a Gaussian lobe of lobe_sigma_deg)
etch.derived: gloss 69 = 69 % of polished glass's flux inside the 60 degree gloss aperture (4.4 x 11.7 degrees); the lobe holds that flux less the specular part
assumed: the gloss is the standard 60 degree geometry (ASTM D523)
the lobe is Gaussian and the same at every angle
the 5151's etch is like Philips' etched display glass
etch.ref: Nuijs & Horikx, Diffraction and scattering at antiglare structures for display devices, Applied Optics 33 (1994) 4058, Table 1 (Philips Research; etched glass)

faceplate.ref: Philips T16 1987: light transmission about 50 % (normal tint), etched anti-glare option

contrast.note: video gain (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the data')

brightness.note: uniform beam on every line (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the entire screen'); fraction of full drive
